headline: Reservations for Hocking Hills Cabins and Campsites
reservation: While entry to Hocking Hills State Park itself does not currently require a timed permit, high-demand lodging including cabins and campsites often requires booking several months in advance. State Nature Preserves like Conkles Hollow have separate management; always verify current access and specific trail rules through the official Ohio Department of Natural Resources portal before travel.

days.title: Gorges and Sandstone Recesses

stops.name: Old Man’s Cave
stops.detail: Explore the multi-level gorge featuring the Upper Falls and unique sandstone formations via a network of stairs and bridges.

stops.name: Ash Cave
stops.detail: Walk the relatively level approach to a massive horseshoe-shaped recess cave and seasonal waterfall.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes total travel; conditions vary by narrow park roads
days.note: Early arrivals are suggested as parking at Old Man’s Cave fills quickly on weekends.

days.title: High Ridges and Rushing Falls

stops.name: Conkles Hollow State Nature Preserve
stops.detail: Choose between the cool, shaded gorge trail or the demanding rim hike for views of the deep sandstone canyon.

stops.name: Cedar Falls
stops.detail: Visit this heavy-flow waterfall where the creek plunges over a mossy cliff face into a rocky basin.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour total; winding rural routes require focused driving
days.note: Rim trails have exposed edges; use caution and stay on marked paths at all times.

days.title: Forest Lakes and Local History

stops.name: Lake Logan State Park
stops.detail: A quieter setting for lakeside walking or birdwatching away from the main gorge crowds.

stops.name: Paul A. Johnson Pencil Sharpener Museum
stops.detail: A brief, quirky stop in Logan to see a unique collection of thousands of historic sharpeners.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; local town traffic can vary
days.note: Lake activities are seasonal; check official boating and swimming rules for current status.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Parking lots at Old Man's Cave and Ash Cave are the most prone to filling by mid-morning. Have a secondary trailhead in mind if your first choice is at capacity.

intel.title: Mobile Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is notoriously inconsistent within the deep sandstone gorges. Download all trail maps and navigation for the Logan and Laurelville areas offline before departing.

intel.title: Regional Refueling
intel.text: Logan and Nelsonville serve as the primary hubs for fuel and groceries. Do not rely on finding services once you enter the immediate state park forest zones.

intel.title: Waterfall Flow
intel.text: Waterfall volume at Cedar Falls and Ash Cave is highly dependent on recent rainfall. Late spring typically offers the most consistent flow compared to the drier summer months.

intel.title: Trail Surfaces
intel.text: Sandstone steps and wooden bridges can become extremely slick after rain. Wear sturdy footwear with significant traction for any route involving stairs.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Rickenbacker International Airport, stock up on supplies in Logan, and check into your cabin or site before dark.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for main park roads; check winter restrictions if visiting during ice season.
plan.goldenHour: Ash Cave offers dramatic lighting in the late afternoon, though deep gorge shadows arrive early depending on the season.
